newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf boosted by stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Elf boosted by stake sale.

text.p: Shares in French oil group Elf Aquitaine rose by more than two percent in a market which was sharply lower after Renault said it had sold its 0.90 percent stake to an Elf unit.
At 0906 GMT, Elf was up 2.17 percent at 611 francs while the CAC-40 index was down 1.01 percent at 2758.23.

Dealers said that they expected Elf to cancel the shares at a later stage, as well as the shares it bought earlier this year from the state. They noted the group would ask authorisation at its May 31 annual general meeting to reduce its share capital by up to 15 percent.
The move would boost earnings per share and the net asset value per share and, in turn, increase the price.

Dealers also noted that there had been rumours about a pending placement of Elf shares and some traders had gone short in the share -- selling more stock than they owned to push the price down ahead of the placement with an idea of buying stock during the placement, making a profit in the process.
These traders now found themselves short of shares and had to buy in the market before the price rose further and turned their short position into a loss.
